name: Zoar Data Center
notes: Data Center Map lists Zoar Data Center at Mihai Eminescu no 2, Buzau, operated by Zoar Online SRL; free listing does not disclose capacity. No other standalone data center facility or project found in Buzau county; the South-East regional data center (Centrul Regional de Date Sud-Est) remains a planned financing call under PR Sud-Est 2021-2027 with no site selected.

name: Centrul de Date Regional Sud-Muntenia (Calarasi participation)
developer: Serviciul de Telecomunicatii Speciale (STS) with Calarasi County Council among partners
notes: Official Calarasi County Council project page (SMIS 342697, PR SM 2021-2027) lists STS in partnership with the county councils of Arges, Calarasi, Dambovita, Giurgiu, Ialomita, Prahova and Teleorman implementing the South-Muntenia Regional Data Center. Total budget 236.4 million lei, implementation July 2025 - December 2028. The physical data center facility is to be built in Prahova county, Ploiesti; Calarasi is a partner county for digital services migration (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS for local public authorities).

name: Tema Energy Data Center Mobil (Resita deployment)
notes: Tema Energy's reference-project page describes a mobile/modular data center (container type) deployed at its operating location in Resita, Caras-Severin, including electrical supply/distribution installation works carried out by the company; small-scale enterprise facility, capacity not disclosed. No large standalone data center project found in Caras-Severin.

name: DriverAI Quantum AI Data Center (Luna)
notes: Announced late May 2026 by Senate president Mircea Abrudean: USD 1 billion first-phase investment for a quantum-AI data center in Luna commune, Cluj county (bordering Mures), on 84 ha of the former 115 ha Tetarom V tech-park land concessioned 2024. PressOne investigation (29 Jun 2026) reports the site is on the banks of the Aries river near Air Base 71 Campia Turzii, the center would be built fully underground, no MoU/agreement signed, operator DriverAI LLC (Arizona, founded Jul 2024) has no prior track record, and the land concession is contested in litigation at Tribunalul Alba. mlq.ai reports a planned 80 MW capacity.

name: efect.RO DC1
notes: Data Center Map and Data Center Catalog list efect.RO DC1 at Str. Jan Huss 29, Cluj-Napoca, offering colocation with redundant power/cooling (APC, IBM/Lenovo, Uniflair equipment); capacity not disclosed in free listings.

name: GTS Cluj-Napoca Data Center
notes: Official GTS page: GTS Cluj data center with N+1 redundant technologies, max installed power 500 kW (est. annual PUE 1.4), current colocation capacity 60 racks with immediate expansion potential. GTS also hosts third-party providers' infrastructure (e.g., NameBox) in this facility.

name: Orange Romania Constanta Data Center
notes: Orange Romania operates a data center in Constanta where solar panels were commissioned in November 2022 (part of ~650 panels across Constanta, Brasov and Timisoara data centers; Orange plans solar at four data centers by 2026). Capacity not disclosed; balcanicaucaso.org article also counts Constanta among Romanian data-center cities (59 locations nationwide).

No substantiated standalone data center project or facility found for Covasna county / Sfantu Gheorghe in targeted searches (Romanian-language searches for centru de date); results were blood-donation centers, cultural/sports projects and other non-IT facilities.

name: Centrul de Date Regional Sud-Muntenia (Dambovita participation)
developer: Serviciul de Telecomunicatii Speciale (STS) with Dambovita County Council among partners
notes: Dambovita County Council is an official partner (with Arges, Calarasi, Giurgiu, Ialomita, Prahova, Teleorman and STS) in the South-Muntenia Regional Data Center project (SMIS 342697, PR SM 2021-2027, total budget 236.4 million lei, Jul 2025 - Dec 2028). The data center facility itself is to be built in Ploiesti, Prahova county; no standalone data center found in Targoviste or elsewhere in Dambovita.

name: ClusterPower Craiova Data Center Campus (Mischii)
notes: ClusterPower inaugurated on 1 April 2022 in Mischii commune, Dolj county (25,427 sqm site) the largest data center in Romania - first hyperscale in South-Eastern Europe - a 25,000 sqm AI one-stop-shop technology park with Nvidia DGX A100 supercomputing, initial investment ~EUR 36-40 million (172 million lei, incl. 82 million lei state aid). Campus plans five data centers fed by an on-site gas-fired power plant of up to 200 MW; direct connection to Transelectrica grid and Transgaz network. Construction of the first of the five centers was ongoing as of 2023 per founder interviews.

name: Orange Romania Galati Data Center (NCC Balcan-IX Galati)
notes: Data Center Map lists the Galati data center of Orange Romania at St. Brailei 41, Galati, with a 2021 M&A timeline event (Telekom Romania Communications / NCC Balcan-IX Galati); free listing does not disclose power capacity. No other standalone data center project found in Galati county.

name: BNR Targu Jiu Data Center (Agenția BNR Gorj)
notes: Constructiv.ro reports BNR received three bids in October 2016 for the fit-out of its data center at the BNR Gorj Agency, Strada Geneva 4, Targu Jiu (budget 15.5 million lei excl. VAT, ~2-year execution). The facility is the central bank's regional backup/disaster-recovery data center and is presumed operational today; capacity not published.
